learning_objective: 🔗 Discover the invisible mathematical ties between things! Learn how to measure if two variables move together, oppose each other, or have no relationship at all.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: सहसंबंध (दो चरों के बीच संबंध या जुड़ाव की माप)
धनात्मक सहसंबंध (जब दो चर एक ही दिशा में बढ़ते या घटते हैं)
ऋणात्मक सहसंबंध (जब एक चर बढ़ता है और दूसरा घटता है)
प्रकीर्ण आरेख / विक्षेप चित्र (बिंदुओं द्वारा सहसंबंध दर्शाने वाला ग्राफ)
गुणांक (सहसंबंध की ताकत को दर्शाने वाली संख्या, -1 से +1 तक)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It measures the relationship between two variables. For example, 'Temperature' and 'Ice cream sales'. If temperature rises, ice cream sales rise. This is a relationship!

Positive: Both move in the SAME direction (e.g., Advertising and Sales). Negative: They move in OPPOSITE directions (e.g., Price of a car and Demand for it). Zero: No relationship at all (e.g., Shoe size and IQ).

A simple visual tool. You plot pairs of variables as dots on an X-Y graph. If the dots form a band moving upwards, it's positive. If they slope downwards, it's negative. If they look like a random cloud of dots, there is no correlation.

A mathematical method to find the exact degree of linear correlation. The answer 'r' always lies strictly between -1 and +1. +1 is a perfect positive relationship, -1 is perfect negative, and 0 means no linear relationship.

Used when data cannot be measured in exact numbers but can be ranked (like beauty, honesty, or judging a painting competition). It calculates the correlation based on the differences in the ranks given to the items.

fun_activity.title: ⚖️ Correlation is NOT Causation!
fun_activity.instructions: Just because two things move together doesn't mean one causes the other. For example, 'Shark attacks' and 'Ice cream sales' both increase in the summer. They are positively correlated. But eating ice cream doesn't cause shark attacks! The hidden 'third variable' causing both is simply the hot weather.

exam_tips: 📌 Always state the range: The coefficient of correlation 'r' can NEVER be greater than 1 or less than -1. (-1 ≤ r ≤ +1).
📌 Karl Pearson's method measures only LINEAR relationships. If the relationship is curved, 'r' might be zero even if they are related.
📌 Spearman's rank correlation formula is: r_s = 1 - [6ΣD² / n(n² - 1)], where D is the difference in ranks.
quick_recap: ⭐ The sign (+ or -) indicates the direction of the relationship, while the number (e.g., 0.8) indicates the strength.
⭐ A correlation of ±0.8 to ±1 is considered 'Highly Correlated'.
⭐ Scatter diagrams give a quick visual idea of the relationship but do not provide an exact mathematical value.
